note: Let terminating old pods finish their in-flight requests (3 s drain + shutdown) so nothing writes NULL any more.

Backfill existing guest orders NULL -> '' in small primary-key ranges, committing after each batch: only short row locks, no long transaction, app traffic unaffected. Single DO statement so the in-block COMMITs are allowed.

Add CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID: enforced for new rows from now on, no table scan. Needs only a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, taken with a short lock_timeout and retried so app queries never queue behind it for long. Skipped if it already exists.
Safety sweep: convert any NULL that slipped in between the backfill and the constraint (e.g. a straggling old pod). Normally updates 0 rows; takes only a ROW EXCLUSIVE lock.
Validate the constraint: full scan under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, which does not block reads or inserts.
SET NOT NULL (Postgres skips the table scan because the valid CHECK proves no NULLs), then drop the now-redundant CHECK. Both in one short transaction with a short lock_timeout and retries.
